solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Day inside, playing endless Pacman is crazy

indicators.note: something without an end has lost its final letter
letters at play are moved about freely, out of their printed order
one thing sitting inside another means it is placed within it

blocks.note: the video game's name with its last letter cut
D is the standard abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Someone staying indoors all day, playing Pacman without end, which is crazy behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Day inside' reads as someone staying indoors; it is the letter D going inside the rearranged game.
explanation.definitionFit: A madcap person or scheme is wildly reckless and impulsive, so the adjective is a straight synonym.

clue.text: McAvoy’s briefly stopped by tedious person guiding festival

indicators.note: said briefly, a word is cut short by its final letter
a thing stopped by something has that something plugged into its middle

blocks.note: James McAvoy is the Scottish actor; his first name loses its last letter
a bore is a tiresome person

explanation.surface: The actor James McAvoy briefly held up by a dull man who is running a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The surname is the misdirection: the letters come from McAvoy's first name, James, the Scottish actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large lively celebration or gathering, such as a Scout rally, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: Came in casually, close to VIP, and dined for free

indicators.note: done casually means done loosely and without order
the close of a word is its very end, its final letter

blocks.note: anagram fodder, six letters
the final letter of VIP
to dine is to eat; past tense

explanation.surface: A gatecrasher strolls in casually, sidles up to a VIP and gets a free meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For free' looks like part of the dinner story, but 'free' is a verb here and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To emancipate is to set someone at liberty, especially from slavery or legal restraint, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Express emotion when Bill’s excluded from coming

indicators.note: what is excluded from a word is left out of it, shortening it

blocks.note: a bill is a poster or advertisement: AD
an advent is an arrival or coming

explanation.surface: Someone gets emotional when Bill is told he is not invited to come along.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill is not a man but a poster, AD; take it from ADVENT and VENT remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To vent feelings is to let anger or frustration out openly, so it matches giving voice to strong feeling.

clue.text: Multi-skilled person led on rural regeneration

indicators.note: regeneration rebuilds things in a new form, so the letters are remade

blocks.note: anagram fodder, ten letters

explanation.surface: A versatile manager heading up a project to revive the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an all-rounder is a player who both bats and bowls well, the usual British sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-rounder is good at many different things, a direct synonym for a versatile, many-talented individual.

clue.text: Boss contracted survey

indicators.note: a contracted word is shortened, here losing its final letter

blocks.note: to study something is to survey or examine it

explanation.surface: A manager has hired someone to carry out a survey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' reads as manager, but it is the raised knob on a shield or a piece of leather.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is also a raised ornamental knob on a surface, which is exactly what a decorative metal stud is.

clue.text: Queen has man in charge cutting pie

indicators.note: a blade cutting into something sits inside it

blocks.note: Qu. is a dictionary abbreviation for queen
a man is a he
i/c is the usual abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: The Queen has a manservant slicing a pie for her.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen is usually a single R or ER; here it is QU, which with the man makes QU-HE for 'in charge' to cut into.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiche is an open savoury tart with an egg custard filling, so a type of pie: an example.

clue.text: Fighter with the French Resistance is welcoming respite

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one part goes inside

blocks.note: w is a standard abbreviation for with
le is French for the
R is the physics symbol for resistance
a rest is a break or respite

explanation.surface: A soldier of the wartime French Resistance is glad of a break from the fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French Resistance' is not one thing: 'the French' and 'Resistance' are separate pieces that surround the respite.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrestler is a combat athlete who grapples an opponent to the mat, so a kind of fighter.

clue.text: Warning sign when gangster with gun strap abruptly left

indicators.note: ending abruptly means being cut off before the last letter

blocks.note: Al Capone, the crossword's stock gangster
a gun is a firearm, an arm
a strap is a belt, cut short
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A gangster with a gun abruptly leaving is a bad omen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abruptly' belongs with the strap, not with 'left': BELT loses its T, then L follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm bells, in the idiom, are a figurative signal that something is wrong, which is what a warning sign is.

clue.text: Nice street in Turkey, or Türkiye, to be more correct

indicators.note: to be in something is to be placed inside it

blocks.note: Nice is the French city, where a street is a rue
TR is the international code for Turkey, now officially Türkiye

explanation.surface: A pedant correcting the name of a country, since Turkey now prefers to be called Türkiye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective. The Türkiye aside is a joke about pedantry that also covers the code TR, which both names share.
explanation.definitionFit: Truer is the comparative of true, and true can mean accurate, so it means closer to accuracy.

clue.text: Senior ministers taking taxi home verges on extravagant

indicators.note: the verges of a word are its edges, its outer letters

blocks.note: a cab is a taxi
at home is in
the first and last letters of extravagant

explanation.surface: Top ministers taking a taxi home, which is bordering on extravagance.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the Cabinet is the group of senior government ministers who run departments under the Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cabinet is the committee of the most senior government ministers, so the collective noun names the group.

clue.text: Lessens blushing by analysis of cues

indicators.note: analysis breaks something down into its parts, which can be rearranged

blocks.note: someone blushing is red-faced
anagram fodder, four letters

explanation.surface: Therapy that studies the triggers of embarrassment makes a person blush less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cues' reads as triggers in the surface; here it is only four letters to rearrange after RED.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce something is to make it smaller or diminish it, so the two verbs are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: For every individual, discount 50%

indicators.note: knocking half off a price here knocks half the letters off a word

blocks.note: an individual is a person; keep the first three of its six letters

explanation.surface: A shop offer: half price for each customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For every individual' looks like one phrase, but the definition stops at 'every'.
explanation.definitionFit: Per is a preposition meaning each or apiece, as in ten pounds a head, so it matches.

clue.text: To cut a long story short, one old lady’s taking on quite regular trade importing heroin

definitions.text: To cut a long story short

indicators.note: regular letters are taken at even intervals, every other one
to import goods is to bring them inside

blocks.note: one as the Roman numeral I
nan is a British word for grandmother
the second and fourth letters of quite
to trade goods is to sell them
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A long tale cut short: a grandmother has taken up drug smuggling on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite regular' is not an adverb and adjective: 'regular' takes every other letter of 'quite'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for summing something up briefly, stating only the essential point in very few words.

clue.text: Rejig of tax ignored grievance

indicators.note: a rejig is a rearrangement, putting things in new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, ten letters

explanation.surface: A tax reform that paid no attention to a public complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end; everything before it is the fodder plus its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Having an axe to grind is an idiom for nursing a private grudge or complaint, so it names a grievance.

clue.text: Cowardy custard threatened young dude

blocks.note: threatened people feel frightened
Y is an abbreviation for young
in jazz slang a cat is a man or dude

explanation.surface: A cowardly youngster who was frightened by a threat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cowardy custard' is a British playground taunt for a coward.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are childish taunts for a timid, fearful person, making them synonyms in the language of the playground.

clue.text: A good clearout’s part of hygiene management

indicators.note: a part of a phrase is a run of letters taken from within it

blocks.note: the letters run across the space between the two words

explanation.surface: Having a thorough clearout is part of managing cleanliness at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clearout' suggests tidying a cupboard; it is the bowel that gets cleared.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema flushes the lower bowel with injected fluid, a cheeky description of a medical flushing procedure.

clue.text: Drive Leo to reveal criminal

indicators.note: to drive things is to push them about, out of their order

blocks.note: Drive doubles as fodder: DRIVE plus LEO, eight letters

explanation.surface: A detective pushes a man called Leo until he exposes the villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' works twice: its letters are fodder and its sense signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An evildoer is someone who does wicked deeds, a broad synonym for a lawbreaker or wrongdoer.

clue.text: Aim to finish

blocks.note: an aim is a goal, as in the phrase means to an ...
to finish is to conclude or stop

explanation.walkthrough: 'Aim to finish' reads as one instruction, but the two words are separate definitions, joined by 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: An end is both a goal, as in means to an end, and the conclusion of something: two distinct senses.

clue.text: Searching for article newspaper’s backtracked on

indicators.note: to backtrack is to go back the way one came, so run backwards

blocks.note: a is the indefinite article
the Financial Times, this very newspaper
re means about or on, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A reporter hunting for a piece the paper has since retracted.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT is the Financial Times, where this puzzle ran.
explanation.definitionFit: To be after something is to be seeking or pursuing it, as in the police are after him.

clue.text: South doesn’t feature in verse about excellent north country

indicators.note: something that does not feature is absent, so it is dropped
turning about means facing the other way, so read backwards

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for south
a stanza is a verse of a poem
A1 means excellent, with the 1 read as I
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A poem about a fine northern land that never mentions the south.
explanation.walkthrough: STANZA without S is TANZA; A1 and N reversed give NIA. 'North country' tempts, but TANZANIA is in East Africa and 'north' is only N.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanzania is a nation in East Africa, bordering Kenya, so it is an example of a sovereign state.

clue.text: Eventually expected to be admitted to popular classes

indicators.note: being admitted means being let inside, so one part goes within another

blocks.note: a baby or train that is expected is due
what is popular is in fashion, in
a series of classes is a course

explanation.surface: A student who hopes one day to get into oversubscribed classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popular classes' reads as one phrase, but the expected word lands between its two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: In due course means at the appropriate time, later on, an idiom that matches finally or in the end.

clue.text: Serve food his horrible party consumes

indicators.note: something horrible is a mess, its letters jumbled
consuming something takes it inside

blocks.note: the DUP, the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland
anagram fodder, three letters

explanation.surface: A caterer serves a dreadful party that wolfs down everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is a Northern Irish political party, hence 'party' as the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To dish up is to put a meal onto plates and bring it to the table, a phrasal verb synonym.

clue.text: Small drink of pop

blocks.note: a small measure of spirits
to pop somewhere is to make a quick trip there

explanation.surface: A sip of fizzy pop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' wants to be a fizzy drink; it is the verb, as in pop to the shops.
explanation.definitionFit: A nip is a dram of spirits, and to nip, like pop, is British for a quick short trip somewhere.

clue.text: Agreed boarding quay’s more cramped

indicators.note: boarding a vessel means getting aboard, inside it

blocks.note: OK means agreed
a pier is a quay or jetty

explanation.surface: Passengers boarding from an overcrowded quayside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boarding' fits the ship picture, but it is OK that goes aboard PIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Poky describes a room that is small and confined, so the comparative means tighter and less spacious.

clue.text: First aider’s bitten by angry spider in distress

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the next word
an angry thing is agitated, thrown into disorder
what is bitten is held between the teeth, inside

blocks.note: anagram fodder, six letters
the first letter of aider

explanation.surface: A first-aider bitten by a furious spider and left in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First aider' is not a medic: 'First' picks the opening A of 'aider', which goes into rearranged SPIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair and distress both name a state of deep unhappiness and anguish, so the nouns are close synonyms.

clue.text: Workers imprisoned by Russian Tsar

indicators.note: held prisoner inside, so the letters sit within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the space between the two words

explanation.surface: Labourers locked up by the Russian emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Workers' is a crossword staple for ants or bees, the worker castes of an insect colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker ants are the sterile females that forage and build for the colony, so they are literally workers.

clue.text: In the past wife always returned

blocks.note: w is the abbreviation for wife
ay or aye is an old word for always
someone returned is back

explanation.surface: Long ago, the wife always came home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' looks like a reversal signal, but it is simply BACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Way back is an informal idiom for a long time ago, as in way back in the sixties.

clue.text: Threadbare argument upheld point

indicators.note: held up in a down entry means turned to read from the bottom upward

blocks.note: a row is a quarrel
a compass point, north

explanation.surface: A tired, overused argument that was nevertheless upheld on appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' is a compass point: N, E, S or W.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare cloth is thin from long use, and worn describes fabric damaged through wear, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Celebrate former soldier getting in university

indicators.note: getting in means being let inside something

blocks.note: ex means former
U is the abbreviation for university
Lt is short for lieutenant, an army officer

explanation.surface: An ex-soldier celebrates being accepted by a university.
explanation.walkthrough: The former soldier is EX-LT, an ex-lieutenant, with U getting in between the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To exult is to rejoice triumphantly, showing great elation, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Sailor’s innermost heart reflected in simple tale

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter
a mirror reflection shows things the other way round
being in something puts it inside

blocks.note: tar, short for tarpaulin, is a sailor
the fifth of the word's nine letters
a simple person is naive

explanation.surface: A sailor's deepest feelings shown in a plain little story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Innermost heart' looks like one idea, but 'heart' takes the middle letter of 'innermost', which joins the sailor before both are reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of connected events, a story, so it is a straight synonym for a tale.
